ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory and systematic screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorised signatories before incorporation and on a continual quarterly basis against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the United States OFAC SDN and consolidated screening lists, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and internationally reputable Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) and adverse-media databases. The screening must be risk-based, fully automated, independently audited, and documented in a compliance file retained for at least five years under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and applicable FMA guidelines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register and Business Name Registry (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirements under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993 and the Companies Regulatory Framework. All company names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet, using ordinary English letters, Arabic numerals, and permitted punctuation symbols. Names containing characters outside the Latin script must be romanised/transliterated into a plain Latin form that accurately represents the intended phonetic name and is not calculated to deceive. Te Reo Māori words are permitted and must be spelled correctly; a proposed name that is likely to be mistaken for an existing registered name, or that falsely implies connection with the Crown, an approver, a State entity, or a particular profession or regulatory status, is prohibited unless prior written approval from the relevant agency is obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection by the Registrar of Companies, the applicant may file a written request for review with the New Zealand Companies Office within 10 working days of the adverse notice, setting out the grounds of objection and any supporting evidence of distinctiveness, consent, or statutory compliance. The Registrar will issue a written decision within 20 working days. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may pursue an administrative appeal to the District Court under the Companies Act 1993, section 22(6), or seek judicial review under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972. The same remedy applies to a failure to extend a reserved name; a reservation may be renewed once for an additional 20 working days by filing a formal extension request and paying the applicable Companies Office fee before the original reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may satisfy the Companies Act 1993 requirement of an address for service and a physical registered office only if the service provider offers a genuine street address in New Zealand that is open during ordinary business hours for the receipt of legal process and mail, and the office is not exclusively a P.O. Box or digital mailbox. However, for a licensed peer-to-peer micro-lending platform subject to FMA supervision under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, a purely virtual office is not permissible. The applicant must maintain a substantive operational presence in New Zealand, including a physical office for records, senior management or an outsourced compliance officer based in New Zealand, and the FMA may require this as part of the licensing assessment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection is above 70% within the first 12 months of proceeding, given the high-risk classification under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the FMA's risk-based supervision programme for non-deposit-taking consumer lenders. The FMA and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand exercise statutory inspection powers and may conduct inspections at the registered office without prior notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) — ss. 10, 11, 12, 13 (incorporation and registration), s. 15 (no par value shares; minimum one share), ss. 20–23 (name restrictions), ss. 28–29 (registered office), ss. 120–127 (constitution), ss. 151–153 (directors and officer consents), ss. 180–184 (company secretary and officer duties), ss. 190–206 (shareholder rights), s. 218 (annual return). Supporting financial-services statutes relevant to the licensed lending scope: Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 Part 6 and Schedule 2 (market services licence for peer-to-peer lending services); Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 (FSP register); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (reporting entity obligations); Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act 2003 (responsible lending). The entity label 'CK_IC (International Company)' is achieved in New Zealand as an ordinary limited-liability company with no minimum capital, non-resident shareholding permitted, and the statutory flexibility to adopt a constitution tailored to offshore trustees; New Zealand does not maintain a separate 'International Companies Act', so the Companies Act 1993 is the exclusive incorporation statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO) — a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the national companies register and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NC1 equivalent — 'Application for Registration of a Company' (statutory form prescribed under s. 12 of the Companies Act 1993) submitted electronically via the Companies Office online incorporation service.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or banked-capital certificate is required in New Zealand. The Act permits shares of no par value and a company may be incorporated with a single share issued fully paid at a nominal NZ$1.00 to the subscriber (s.15 Companies Act 1993). Share capital may be fully subscribed by board resolution after incorporation; the Companies Office does not verify capital deposits. The only governance conditions are the appointment of at least one director resident in New Zealand (s.151(2)) and maintenance of a registered office in New Zealand (s.128).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED

RECITALS: The Company was duly incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) on [DATE], registered under NZBN [NUMBER]; its registered office is at [ADDRESS], New Zealand; the constitution of the Company (or the default rules of the Companies Act 1993, where no constitution is adopted) forms the governance contract.

IT IS RESOLVED AND RECORDED UNANIMOUSLY BY THE FOUNDING DIRECTORS:
1. Incorporation and Share Capital. The registration of the Company, the adoption of the constitution, and the allotment to the subscriber of [X] ordinary shares of no par value issued as fully paid for NZ$[AMOUNT] per share, without any escrow deposit or minimum paid-up capital endorsement, are confirmed and ratified.
2. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company shall be maintained at [ADDRESS], New Zealand, open to the public at the hours required by s.128 of the Companies Act 1993; the officers are directed to file the registered-office particulars with the New Zealand Companies Office.
3. Directors and Officers. The following appointments are effective immediately: [NAME] as Managing Director; [NAME] as Finance Director; [NAME] as Company Secretary; and [NAME] as AML/CFT Compliance Officer; each director having provided a signed consent to act under s.152 of the Companies Act 1993.
4. Banking, Settlement and Payment Rails. The Board approves the opening of a corporate bank account with [BANK], enrolment for Direct Debit (BECS) facility, and activation of local e-wallet payout rails, and authorises the Managing Director to execute banking mandates and payment-scheme agreements.
5. Financial Licensing Programme. The Board directs management to (i) register the Company as a financial service provider under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 within 10 working days; (ii) join the approved dispute resolution scheme of Financial Services Complaints Limited (FSCL); (iii) file the application with the Financial Markets Authority for a market services licence to operate a peer-to-peer lending service under Part 6 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; and (iv) adopt the AML/CFT compliance programme and appoint the compliance officer under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
6. Responsible Lending. The Company shall register under the Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act 2003 (CCCFA) and adopt the responsible-lending policy and algorithmic-underwriting audit protocol applicable to its micro-loan business.
7. Premises and Occupational Clearance. The officers shall obtain, prior to operational go-live, the building consent and Code Compliance Certificate (if fit-out changes are required), the Building Warrant of Fitness with an appointed Independent Qualified Person, the Fire and Emergency New Zealand evacuation scheme approval (if required by the Fire Safety and Evacuation of Buildings Regulations 2006), and the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 workplace clearance at [ADDRESS].
8. Execution and General Authority. Any two directors, or one director together with the Company Secretary, are authorised to execute documents, affix the common seal (if adopted), and perform all acts ancillary to the above resolutions.

DATED [DATE]. 
[SIGNATURES OF ALL DIRECTORS]

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) — Te Tari Taake; taxpayer portal: myIR (www.ird.govt.nz); corporate registry interface: New Zealand Companies Office and New Zealand Business Number Register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz / www.nzbn.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident international company must: (1) obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) through the Companies Office if engaged in commercial activity in New Zealand, or register manually with the NZBN Register; (2) apply to Inland Revenue for a non-resident IRD number by filing Form IR742 (Non-Resident Company Registration), including the certificate of incorporation, registered office address, director and shareholder details, global ultimate parent details if any, and confirmation of the New Zealand tax compliance status or permanent establishment assessment; (3) if carrying on a financial services business (including peer-to-peer lending), obtain a Financial Service Provider (FSP) registration number under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and include it in Inland Revenue and anti-money laundering compliance filings. For a pure offshore entity without New Zealand-sourced income, IRD issues an IRD number for withholding-tax compliance and GST registration evaluation within approximately 5–10 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: The CK_IC International Company is treated as a non-resident company outside the New Zealand net for income tax purposes; it is taxable only on New Zealand-sourced income, principal among which is interest derived from New Zealand-resident borrowers and any platform fees with a New Zealand source. No New Zealand capital gains tax or wealth tax applies. For indirect tax purposes, the entity is outside the GST system unless it supplies taxable goods or services in New Zealand in the course of a carried-on taxable activity, or it supplies 'remote services' to New Zealand resident consumers and exceeds the NZD 60,000 registration threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no check-the-box classification election. The closest equivalent mechanisms are: (i) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 (Form IR427), available only to New Zealand-resident-owned closely held companies and therefore not available to a non-resident international company; (ii) election to treat an offshore branch or fixed establishment of a non-resident company as a permanent establishment under the applicable double tax agreement for tax attribution purposes; (iii) hybrid mismatch notification obligations under Subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007 (Form IR1047), applying to structured hybrid arrangements involving New Zealand parties, consistent with OECD BEPS Action 2, which disallows deductions for payments that are non-taxable in the other jurisdiction; and (iv) the 'associated persons' and CFC disclosure elections that may be required in Form IR1156 for non-resident-controlled entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 for domestic taxable supplies (s 51 GST Act 1985); NZD 60,000 for non-resident suppliers of remote services or distance-selling of goods (ss 54(1)(c) and 54B); a lower NZD 60,000 aggregated threshold applies across all taxable supplies. Credit, lending, and financial intermediary services are exempt financial supplies (s 14 and s 3 GST Act 1985) and therefore do not trigger registration unless the platform also makes taxable supplies such as technology access fees, software subscriptions, or administrative service charges exceeding the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance system, mandatory digital stamping, or government pre-approval of invoices exists in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the Peppol interoperability framework administered by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE). A GST-registered supplier must issue a tax invoice within 28 days of the time of supply, unless a buyer-created tax invoice arrangement is in place. There is no API-based transaction clearance portal; IRD relies on periodic GST returns (filed monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly) and post-event audit rather than continuous transaction validation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is claimable under s 11(1) of the GST Act 1985 for goods physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of supply, and under s 11A for services supplied to a non-resident recipient outside New Zealand, provided the supply is not made to an individual who receives it for private consumption in New Zealand and is not directly connected with land or goods situated in New Zealand at the time of supply. For a P2P micro-lending platform, loan origination, credit facilitation, and loan administration fees constitute exempt financial supplies and are excluded from zero-rating; however, separately invoiced platform services, merchant consulting, or technology-as-a-service subscriptions supplied to non-resident borrowers, lenders, or partner institutions may qualify for zero-rating under s 11A if the recipient is outside New Zealand and the services are not physically performed in New Zealand or connected to New Zealand real property.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged via the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window or Safe Management System (CUSR clearance reference)
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or equivalent multimodal transport document evidencing physical departure from New Zealand within 28 days of the supply date
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment confirmation (SWIFT MT103 / correspondent bank credit advice) evidencing receipt of export consideration in the exporter's bank account
Supplier's GST tax invoice prepared in accordance with s 24 of the GST Act 1985, including the zero-rating statement where required
Contractual documentation, purchase orders, or signed service agreements demonstrating the non-resident status of the recipient and absence of a New Zealand private-consumption nexus
Where related-party export pricing is involved, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and a comparability analysis satisfying s GC 13 of the Income Tax Act 2007
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is referenced as the international commercial norm and as an IRD audit indicator for cross-border cash-flow substance. Failure to substantiate zero-rating exposes the taxpayer to: (i) an assessment shortfall penalty of 20% for unacceptable tax position, up to 150% for evasion or similar act under s 141E of the Tax Administration Act 1994; (ii) late payment penalties of 1% per month and use-of-money interest at the current rate of 9.15% per annum; (iii) criminal prosecution under s 143A for knowingly providing false or misleading GST documentation, punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to NZD 50,000 for individuals or NZD 100,000 for companies; (iv) retrospective clawback of all GST refunds under s 26(3) of the GST Act 1985 where a supply is found not to have been actually exported or not supplied to the stated offshore recipient; and (v) the statutory four-year time bar for reassessment (s 108 Tax Administration Act 1994) does not protect a taxpayer where fraud, evasion, or misleading conduct is established. Additionally, for the P2P lending platform, the Financial Markets Authority may impose civil penalties of up to the greater of NZD 1 million or three times the gain for unlicensed market intermediary activities under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand may pursue anti-money-laundering enforcement action under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) as the central monetary authority; foreign exchange and cross-border payment oversight also involves the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for derivative and financial services licensing, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade for any residual sanctions and trade remittance policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full convertibility on both the current account and the capital account. There is no general foreign exchange control law, no requirement to obtain central bank approval before making external payments or receipts, and no statutory distinction between current and capital transactions for convertibility purposes. All NZD and foreign-currency bank accounts may be freely serviced in-country and offshore. Dividend remittances, capital repatriation, loan principal and interest payments, and platform fee remittances are unrestricted, subject only to New Zealand non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) or approved issuer levy, transfer pricing documentation, and thin capitalization rules under the Income Tax Act 2007. For an International Company classified as a Tax Exempt Zone entity, no additional exchange-control clearance is required beyond the standard commercial bank anti-money-laundering documentation for each wire transfer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no prescribed timeline for bringing export or other foreign-currency receipts onshore. The Reserve Bank does not impose any forced swap to NZD. The only practical obligations are (a) transactional reporting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 when a currency transaction exceeds NZD 10,000 or triggers a prescribed transaction report, and (b) statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the Reserve Bank if external financial assets or liabilities exceed applicable threshold amounts. The International Company may hold export-like trade proceeds in any currency indefinitely.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, with material legal constraints. Offshore digital EMI and non-bank electronic money institutions (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Currencycloud) can provide virtual IBAN and multi-currency settlement rails, but they do not hold a New Zealand banking licence and cannot independently offer local New Zealand clearing accounts. To operate in New Zealand, an offshore EMI must either be registered as a Financial Service Provider (FSP) with the Financial Markets Authority and comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, or rely on a locally regulated payment partner or outsourced AML/CFT provider. For the P2P micro-lending platform, the only fully compliant route is to maintain a primary relationship with a tier-1 domestic bank for the capital escrow and disbursement accounts, while using an FMA-registered local payment gateway (or an EMI that has obtained a New Zealand money remittance licence) for ACH Direct Debit and Local Wallet Payout rail connections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand statutes do not mandate a physical branch interview for corporate account openers; the AML/CFT framework allows non-face-to-face verification if electronic identity proofing meets the supervisors' standards. However, for a non-resident International Company with no physical presence in New Zealand, a tier-1 bank will normally require either (a) an in-person interview at a New Zealand branch attended by at least one director or authorized signatory, or (b) a certified simultaneous video interview supported by notarized corporate documents, APOSTILLE-certified certificates of incorporation, current register of directors and shareholders, a board resolution authorizing account opening, and original or certified identification for each beneficial owner and signatory. Practical viability for remote-only opening is Low; a physical or high-integrity virtual interview is effectively mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk lending classification under ISIC 6499 without a clear local lending licence or robust AML/CFT programme
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the FMA licence or registration as a peer-to-peer lending service under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; dedicated AML/CFT compliance manual approved by the appointed NZ compliance officer; resume and appointment letter of the AML/CFT compliance officer; independent audit report confirming adherence to AML/CFT procedure; algorithmic underwriting whitepaper and borrower KYC flow; sample loan agreements and disclosure statements; transactional velocity and limits policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident International Company with no commercial substance or physical office in New Zealand
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation and memorandum of association; current certificate of good standing; board resolution establishing a registered New Zealand service address; executed office lease or serviced-office agreement; employment agreements of at least two local compliance and operations staff; functional substance report detailing treasury, AML/CFT, and risk governance; proof of delegation of payment operations to a licensed NZ provider; CRS/FATCA entity classification form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth or unexplained cross-border capital injection via MT103 wires
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 transaction records showing exact purpose codes; detailed source-of-wealth statements for each beneficial owner and funding entity; audited financial statements of the funding shareholder or investor; twelve months of bank statements of the funding source; IRD tax clearance certificate; CRS and FATCA declarations; signed board minutes confirming the amount, nature, and purpose of the inbound capital; legal source of funds opinion from an NZ-qualified counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value disbursements to retail borrowers or local digital wallets, potentially considered money laundering or loan-sharking
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Whitelist framework of approved borrower wallet and account endpoints; transaction velocity and frequency limits for each borrower; direct-debit mandate agreements with an NZ authorized bank; automated AML/CFT transaction monitoring logs; fraud-detection system output; audit trail of all API calls and privileged system access; periodic independent compliance review; regulatory reports filed with FMA and the Police Financial Intelligence Unit as required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must be routed through a SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for nostro/internal transfers) into the International Company's tier-1 New Zealand bank account, using the beneficiary account name as per the bank records, the beneficiary New Zealand bank account number and BIC, and the correct purpose statement, e.g., 'Loan platform capital injection and working capital'. The sending institution must be provided with (i) the corporate certificate of incorporation, (ii) the board resolution approving the capital contribution, (iii) the FATCA/CRS self-certification, (iv) KYC identification for all beneficial owners, and (v) the source-of-funds documentation, so that the receiving bank can complete the credit to the Capital Escrow Account without delay. Inbound transfers equivalent to USD 1,000,000 or more may trigger enhanced due diligence, but there is no central bank approval threshold. The funds must be booked in a separate escrow ledger account and reconciled against the lending algorithm's capital pool. If the inbound amount represents direct foreign investment in a NZ entity or sensitive land/asset purchase, the Overseas Investment Act 2005 may require a consent, but a pure portfolio contribution or loan to an offshore vehicle is exempt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for loan disbursements, platform fees, and intercompany treasury flows uses (a) for domestic NZD payments: the local NZ Clearing System and the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) via standard ACH Direct Debit and batch EFT rails; (b) for cross-border disbursements: SWIFT MT103 with a clear purpose code such as 'consumer loan disbursement', 'loan repayment', or 'platform service fee', including the overseas beneficiary's full account details and any required FMA transaction reporting; and (c) for larger trade settlements where a documentary credit is required: a SWIFT MT700 commercial letter of credit issued by the tier-1 bank on the IC's account. Each disbursement instruction must reference a unique transaction ID generated by the core lending system, and must be captured in an ISO 20022 XML format for reconciliation with the escrow ledger and tax reporting systems.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forwards (deliverable) up to 12-month tenors
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic or illiquid cross-currency pairs where deliverability is restricted by local counterparty constraints
Cross-currency swaps (basis swaps) for refinancing mismatches between NZD funding obligations and USD/CNH lending proceeds
FX options (calls, puts, collars and zero-cost collars) for contingent exposure on loan prepayments and early repayment risk
FX swaps (swap/swap transactions) for short-term liquidity parking and rollover of intercompany borrowings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 working days after the company's annual return date (anniversary of incorporation, or a board-selected date previously approved by the Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate late-filing penalty of NZD 100 (approx. USD 62); continued non-filing after two consecutive annual return periods allows the Registrar to strike the company off the register after notice of intention to remove, with consequential loss of separate legal personality and enforcement rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: FSPR Annual Confirmation (Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Service Providers Register (administered by the New Zealand Companies Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual confirmation date, being the anniversary of the FSP registration and within 15 working days after that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Removal of the provider from the FSP Register upon non-confirmation, immediately terminating the entity's authority to provide financial services in New Zealand; continued provision of services while unregistered is an offence under the FSP Act with fines up to NZD 30,000 (approx. USD 18,600) for a body corporate and NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,200) for an individual.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Compliance Report (Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (NZ) - AML/CFT Supervisor for licensed peer-to-peer lending service providers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 working days after the end of the reporting entity's financial year, or the 12-month AML/CFT reporting period approved by the supervisor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the AMLCFT Act; conviction may result in a fine of up to NZD 50,000 (approx. USD 31,000) for an individual and NZD 100,000 or more (approx. USD 62,000 or more) for a body corporate, plus civil penalty orders, public censure, suspension or revocation of the P2P licence, and additional supervisory intervention by the FMA.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered for any entity classified as an FMC reporting entity, any licensed P2P lending service provider (as a condition of the FMA licence), and any company meeting the Companies Act 1993 'large company' thresholds (total assets exceeding NZD 60 million or total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million). Smaller non-reporting companies may be audit-exempt but must still prepare general purpose financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) for FMC reporting entities and large for-profit entities; simplified New Zealand GAAP / Simple Format Reporting for smaller non-reporting entities under the External Reporting Board framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate public UBO register; however, each annual return to the Companies Office must accurately reflect the Register of Members, updated for any share transfers during the year. For financial-services licensees, the FSPR annual confirmation and the AML/CFT annual report require the entity to reconfirm its ultimate beneficial owner(s), senior managers and 25% or more controlling shareholders, and to update those records within the prescribed statutory periods after any transfer or change in control.

stage_6.entry_description: Total gross income derived from the P2P lending platform's business operations, including loan origination fees, servicing fees, net interest margin, and any platform facilitation income. All amounts in NZD.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents carrying on business through a NZ fixed establishment must return only income sourced in NZ. Foreign-source lending income not attributable to the NZ PE is excluded. If the company is a NZ resident (incorporated in NZ), worldwide income is assessable at 28%.
